text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion (A) and other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : Time period of oscillation of a liquid drop depends on surface tension (S), if density of the liquid is $ρ$ and radius of the drop is r, then $\mathrm{T}=\mathrm{K}\sqrt{ρ\mathrm{r}^{3}/\mathrm{S}^{3/2}}$ is dimensionally correct, where K is dimensionless.

Reason (R) : Using dimensional analysis we get R.H.S. having different dimension than that of time period.

In the light of above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know,

$\begin{array}{l} [S]=\left [\mathrm{MT}^{-2}\right ] \\  \\ [ρ]=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{-3}\right ] \\  \\ [r]=[\mathrm{L}] \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \therefore \text{Dimension of}\mathrm{RHS} & =\dfrac{\left [\mathrm{M}^{\frac{1}{2}}\mathrm{L}^{-\frac{3}{2}}\right ]\left [\mathrm{L}^{\frac{3}{2}}\right ]}{\left [\mathrm{MT}^{-2}\right ]^{\frac{3}{4}}} \\  \\ =\left [\mathrm{M}^{\left (\frac{1}{2}-\frac{3}{4}\right )}\mathrm{L}^{\left (-\frac{3}{2}+\frac{3}{2}\right )}\mathrm{T}^{\frac{6}{4}}\right ]=\mathrm{M}^{-\frac{1}{4}}\mathrm{L}^{0}\mathrm{T}^{\frac{3}{2}} \end{array}$

dimension of L.H.S. = $[\mathrm{T}]$

$\therefore$ Dimension of LHS $\neq$ Dimension of RHS.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift

text: A ball is thrown up vertically with a certain velocity so that, it reaches a maximum height h. Find the ratio of the times in which it is at height $\frac{h}{3}$ while going up and coming down respectively.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A ball is thrown vertically upward with a certain velocity, reaching a maximum height $h$. We need to find the ratio of the times it is at height $\frac{h}{3}$ while ascending and descending, respectively.

The initial velocity of the ball $v$ can be given by:

$v=\sqrt{2gh}$

When the ball is at height $\frac{h}{3}$, the equation of motion is:

$\frac{h}{3}=\sqrt{2gh}\cdot t-\frac{1}{2}gt^{2}$

Rearranging the equation, we get a quadratic equation in terms of $t$:

$\frac{g}{2}t^{2}-\sqrt{2gh}\cdot t+\frac{h}{3}=0$

The ratio of the times taken to ascend and descend to the height $\frac{h}{3}$ can be found using the quadratic formula solution for $t$, considering the corresponding velocities:

$\frac{t_{1}}{t_{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{2gh}-\sqrt{2gh-\frac{2gh}{3}}}{\sqrt{2gh}+\sqrt{2gh-\frac{2gh}{3}}}$

Simplifying the terms inside the fraction:

$=\frac{\sqrt{2}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}}{\sqrt{2}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift

text: The time period of oscillation of a simple pendulum of length L suspended from the roof of a vehicle, which moves without friction down an inclined plane of inclination $α$, is given by :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The vehicle slides down the frictionless incline with acceleration $a=g\sin α$ along the incline.

In the frame of the vehicle, the bob experiences $⃗{g}_{\text{eff}}=⃗{g}-⃗{a}$. The component of $⃗{g}$ along the incline, $g\sin α$, is cancelled by $-⃗{a}$, leaving only the component perpendicular to the incline:

$g_{\text{eff}}=g\cos α$

The pendulum oscillates about the normal to the incline with time period

$T=2π\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g_{\text{eff}}}}=2π\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g\cos α}}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift

text:
A spherically symmetric charge distribution is considered with charge density varying as

$ρ(r)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} ρ_{0}\left (\frac{3}{4}-\frac{r}{R}\right ) & \text{for}r\leq R \\ \text{zero} & \text{for}r>R \end{array} \right.$

Where, $r(r<R)$ is the distance from the centre O (as shown in figure). The electric field at point P will be:


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By spherical symmetry the field at P is radial, so Gauss's law over a sphere of radius $r$ through P gives

$E(4πr^{2})=\dfrac{Q_{\text{in}}}{ε_{0}}$

Charge enclosed, with $r^{'}$ as the variable of integration:

$Q_{\text{in}}=\int\limits _{0}^{r}ρ_{0}\left (\dfrac{3}{4}-\dfrac{r^{'}}{R}\right )4πr^{'2}dr^{'}=4πρ_{0}\left (\dfrac{r^{3}}{4}-\dfrac{r^{4}}{4R}\right )=πρ_{0}r^{3}\left (1-\dfrac{r}{R}\right )$

Therefore

$E=\dfrac{πρ_{0}r^{3}}{4πε_{0}r^{2}}\left (1-\dfrac{r}{R}\right )=\dfrac{ρ_{0}r}{4ε_{0}}\left (1-\dfrac{r}{R}\right )$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift

text: Two metallic wires of identical dimensions are connected in series. If $σ_{1}$ and $σ_{2}$ are the conductivities of these wires respectively, the effective conductivity of the combination is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Identical dimensions: each wire has length $l$ and cross-sectional area $A$, so $R_{1}=\dfrac{l}{σ_{1}A}$ and $R_{2}=\dfrac{l}{σ_{2}A}$.

Joined end to end in series, they form one conductor of length $2l$ and area $A$ with resistance $R_{1}+R_{2}$. Its effective conductivity $σ$ satisfies

$\dfrac{2l}{σA}=\dfrac{l}{σ_{1}A}+\dfrac{l}{σ_{2}A}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{2}{σ}=\dfrac{1}{σ_{1}}+\dfrac{1}{σ_{2}}\Rightarrow σ=\dfrac{2σ_{1}σ_{2}}{σ_{1}+σ_{2}}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift

text:
A coil of inductance 1 H and resistance $100\Omega$ is connected to a battery of 6 V. Determine approximately :

(a) The time elapsed before the current acquires half of its steady - state value.

(b) The energy stored in the magnetic field associated with the coil at an instant 15 ms after the circuit is switched on. (Given $\ln 2=0.693,\mathrm{e}^{-3/2}=0.25$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The current in the LR circuit grows as

$i(t)=\dfrac{V}{R}\left (1-e^{-t/τ}\right ),τ=\dfrac{L}{R}=\dfrac{1}{100}\text{s}=10\text{ms}$

For half the steady value, $e^{-t/τ}=\dfrac{1}{2}$:

$t=τ\ln 2=10\times 0.693=6.93\text{ms}\approx 7\text{ms}$

At $t=15\text{ms}$, $t/τ=3/2$:

$i=\dfrac{6}{100}\left (1-e^{-3/2}\right )=0.06\times 0.75=0.045\text{A}$

$U=\dfrac{1}{2}Li^{2}=\dfrac{1}{2}\times 1\times (0.045)^{2}=1.01\times 10^{-3}\text{J}\approx 1\text{mJ}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift

text: If the potential barrier across a p-n junction is $0.6\mathrm{V}$. Then the electric field intensity, in the depletion region having the width of $6\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{m}$, will be $__________$ $\times 10^{5}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{C}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The barrier potential $V=0.6\text{V}$ acts across the depletion region of width $d=6\times 10^{-6}\text{m}$, and the field in this region is taken as uniform.

$E=\dfrac{V}{d}=\dfrac{0.6}{6\times 10^{-6}}=1\times 10^{5}\text{N C}^{-1}$

Hence, the answer is 1.
